name: ClickClue – Session Replay
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
See how visitors use your WordPress website. Replay eligible signed-out visits, including pages, clicks and scrolling, inside your dashboard.

Recordings stay in WordPress, never sent to ClickClue or external analytics. Free needs no account or licence key.

What you can do with ClickClue Free

  • Replay visitor sessions: use playback controls and jump to click markers or grouped scroll events.
  • Find useful visits: filter by page, device, date, watched status or bookmark; save filters.
  • Save evidence: bookmark recordings and add review notes.
  • Manage recordings together: select visits to bookmark, mark watched or delete; preview cleanup of recordings lasting 5 seconds or less. Recent uploads and bookmarks stay protected from short-recording cleanup.
  • Control visitor recording: choose the mode, sampling, retention and storage budget.
  • Protect sensitive content: use form-text masking, exclusions, private regions and optional all-text masking.

Investigate navigation, scrolling and routes to forms. Replay cannot establish why someone left.

No trial expiry or monthly quota. Hosting, privacy choices and capture limits apply.

Three ways to start recording

New installs start paused with no mode preselected:

  • Ask with ClickClue’s banner: show the built-in replay prompt. Requires a published privacy policy selected in WordPress.
  • Use my existing consent banner: wait for permission from a banner connected to ClickClue’s local consent API. Installing another banner alone does not connect it.
  • Record without asking first: start eligible visits under the site owner’s chosen policy. This is not a visitor consent decision.

Setup also asks where visitors can stop recording and whether to use unlimited plugin storage or your own budget. The floating privacy button stays off unless chosen; your own footer/menu or connected control is equally available. Save & enable recording enables your chosen mode. Refusals, opt-outs, Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control apply in every mode. Settings alone do not establish legal compliance.

Optional ClickClue Pro add-on

Pro is a separate paid add-on for heatmaps, grouped clues, structural form insights, journeys, comparisons, feedback and team tools. Free works independently. Pro feedback/order integrations require visitor consent.

Compare Free and Pro | Documentation

Useful alongside ClickClue

Optional companions by Plugins.shop:

  • KillerConversions — Build enquiry forms with entries stored in WordPress.
  • Logged.ai — Check supported WordPress changes when investigating a new problem.
  • CampaignBars — Publish targeted announcements, offers and calls to action.
  • Frictions — Dedicated checkout session replay and issue review for WooCommerce stores.

Separate plugins; no automatic integration. See More Plugins for the catalogue.

Privacy and local storage

Public design asset capture is on for fresh installations and off on upgrades until explicitly enabled. Separate SVG files require PHP DOM. Safe SVG geometry can remain; SVG scripts and foreign content, canvas, audio/video, frames, hidden inputs and editable content are excluded. URL query values/fragments are removed except verified public post/page IDs. Structural classes/IDs can remain; exclude sensitive content and attributes with selectors or data-tw-block.

Free does not intentionally collect raw IPs, request bodies, console logs or customer/order IDs. A rotating keyed IP hash temporarily limits uploads; hosting logs are separate. Unsent events stay in memory, capped at 8 MiB with compressed uploads (2 MiB for legacy transport), and clear on withdrawal.

Built-in consent choices last 180 days. Notice, mode or scope changes can require fresh permission, including image approvals or relevant Pro changes. Valid refusals remain respected. Recording basis and acceptance times report what the client asserted and what the server accepted; they do not prove a human decision. Keep independent notice/CMP records when needed. The floating Replay privacy button is optional and off by default. Setup asks you to choose it or confirm your own footer/menu or connected control. A same-page #clickclue-privacy link opens the controls where ClickClue runs. Test stopping and deleting the current recording while signed out; declaring a custom control is not an automatic verification. Existing installations show a reminder without silently turning the button on.

Public design capture saves eligible public WordPress image/font files and safe SVG assets into shared local snapshots. Original public image metadata may remain. Turning this option off stops new copies; existing snapshots follow recording deletion and retention. For Google Fonts already used by a page, its public stylesheet may be reread from fonts.googleapis.com in the browser without cookies or referrer, and font binaries copied from fonts.gstatic.com on the server. Google receives the respective browser/server IP and font request, never recording contents; Google privacy and terms apply. No other arbitrary visitor-provided URL is fetched. Trusted CDN aliases can map to existing local files through the documented developer filter. Private regions take priority. Legacy individually approved images remain supported. Old recordings cannot recover text or assets that were never saved. Review exports separately.

Tutorials, previews, dismissals, companion checks and optional review counters stay local. Admin preferences support privacy export/erasure; selected previews expire after seven days. Links open on selection without site, user or recording identifiers.

Offline Help is included. Translations fall back to English. See BUILD.txt and THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate ClickClue from Plugins > Add New, or upload the clickclue ZIP.
  2. Choose a mode and review privacy/storage settings. For the built-in banner, select a published policy under Settings > Privacy. Existing-banner integration is explained in Help.
  3. Select Save & enable recording. Setup saves 100% sampling until you change it; earlier steps do not enable recording.
  4. Clear page/CDN caches. Open the test link in a signed-out private window, follow your chosen mode, then click and scroll.
  5. Check your test replay and masking. Set your intended sampling rate afterward, or pause recording.

Activate per site; no network activation.

Updating to 1.2.6

  1. Back up your site. Update ClickClue Free first, then the matching Pro add-on if installed, without uninstalling. Pro 1.2.6 requires Free 1.2.6. Reload open admin tabs after updating.
  2. Clear page/CDN caches so visitors receive the current recorder. Existing recordings, settings and licence state are preserved; an upgrade does not choose a new recording mode for you.
  3. Review Settings > Recording & privacy. Cart and checkout are excluded by default. Deliberately including them requires Mask all page text. Confirm where visitors can stop recording: the optional floating button, your footer/menu link or a connected privacy control.
  4. Review Storage & retention. Keep your existing budget or explicitly choose unlimited plugin storage. Hosting capacity still applies. Retention 0 means manual deletion.
  5. Use Test a recording in a signed-out private window. Confirm an upload, watch the replay, check masking, and test stopping and deleting the current session. Restore your intended sampling rate after the test.

Public design asset capture stays off on upgrades until explicitly enabled. Enable it in Settings if you want eligible public images, fonts and design assets saved for new recordings. Keep all-text masking enabled if that is your intended policy.

Legacy recordings that cannot reliably distinguish every form-text change have all page text masked. Version 1.2.4 also filters saved CSS before replay and cleans older stored CSS in bounded background batches through WP-Cron and admin visits. Clicks, scrolling, notes and bookmarks remain. Backups and exported copies are not rewritten.
sections.faq:
Why am I not seeing recordings?

Finish setup and test signed out at 100% sampling. Banner modes need permission. Clear caches; use Test a recording to check privacy signals, exclusions, storage and uploaded activity.

Are typed values or signed-in visitors recorded?

Signed-in visitors and account, login, administration, order-pay and order-confirmation pages are excluded. Form values and descendant text are masked before upload and checked again before storage and replay, including scripted textarea changes. In new recordings, public page text can remain readable when Mask all page text is off. Exclude sensitive content and inspect a test replay.

Can I use it with WooCommerce?

Yes, for eligible signed-out browsing. Cart and checkout are excluded by default, including configured WooCommerce pages and plain permalinks. The advanced Include cart and checkout pages option requires Mask all page text; test your actual theme and gateway with sample details. Account, order-pay and order-confirmation pages remain excluded. Other public pages can also display personal text outside form fields: mask or exclude those regions. Free does not provide customer identification, revenue attribution or guaranteed checkout coverage.

What are the recording and storage limits?

Before setup: paused, 10% sampling and seven-day retention. Setup changes sampling to 100% and requires an explicit storage choice: 0 for no plugin budget, or your own positive budget. Set retention to 0 for manual deletion, or choose a cleanup period. Existing saved budgets and retention are preserved. Long visits are uploaded in batches and replayed in sections, without the former 8 MiB per-visit cutoff. Individual uploads, playback sections, request rates and host resources still have technical safeguards. PHP zlib enables compressed uploads.

Capture pauses at an owner-configured storage budget. Database overhead/backups need extra space. Retries count toward upload limits. Shared proxies/NAT share an allowance; trusted real-client addressing is the host’s responsibility.

Does the consent API call ClickClue’s website?

No. In existing-banner mode, your local integration calls window.ClickClue.grantConsent() after replay acceptance and window.ClickClue.withdrawConsent() on refusal/withdrawal. See Help. Permission is still required.

Why can a replay look different or end early?

Replay reconstructs the recorded page and interactions. Public design capture preserves eligible images, backgrounds, fonts and safe SVG geometry. Private or unavailable assets, video and embedded frames remain excluded. Abrupt closure can lose unsent events despite bounded retries. Replay labels interrupted/unconfirmed delivery. Test your theme and hosting; exact rendering in every browser is not guaranteed.

How do deletion and retention work?

Withdrawal stops capture, clears unsent events and requests deletion of the current valid session. Failed deletion stays pending; dismissal does not confirm deletion. Older sessions follow retention/admin deletion. Hourly WP-Cron needs a real cron trigger on low-traffic sites. Deactivation keeps data; Delete data when uninstalling controls removal.
sections.changelog:
1.2.6

  • Start capture without waiting for optional public font styles, and overlap recorder loading with server authorization after sampling permits the visit.
  • Include clicks on eligible public or approved images while preserving private regions, masking and image-source filtering.
  • Load validated saved fonts under security policies that permit data fonts but block blob fonts; keep replay isolated from live websites.

1.2.5

  • Prevent an older Settings tab or simultaneous save from overwriting newer recording and privacy choices. Keep the draft and offer an explicit reload.
  • Prioritize final upload checkpoints, avoid duplicate background handoffs, and distinguish recent activity from an unconfirmed final checkpoint.
  • Include the configured public WooCommerce placeholder image while retaining private-attachment protections.
  • Preview recording identities before deletion and show date-filter errors beside the fields without reporting a recording-health failure.
  • Reject saved-filter names that become empty after removing markup.

1.2.4

  • Sanitize CSS text and URLs before storage and when reading older recordings; retain the player privacy check.
  • Enforce server-side sampling admission and describe permission records as client-reported signals.
  • Exclude cart and checkout by default; deliberate inclusion requires full page-text masking.
  • Ask separately where visitors can stop recording and whether to use unlimited plugin storage or a positive budget. Preserve existing budgets and the optional default-Off floating button.
  • Correct tutorial and help guidance for long recordings, storage and privacy-control placement.

1.2.3

  • Select recordings together to delete, bookmark or mark watched.
  • Preview and clean up recordings of 5 seconds or less; recent uploads and bookmarks stay protected.
  • Sort recordings, use quick date/review filters, inspect upload details and enable optional automatic refresh.

1.2.2

  • Make the floating Replay privacy button optional and off by default, independently of the recording mode.
  • Add a settings switch, footer/menu privacy links and a local openPrivacy() API.
  • Keep the selected consent banner, visitor choices, masking and stop-and-delete behavior.

1.2.1

  • Correct recording durations and checkpoint seeking when the visitor and server clocks differ.
  • Combine large snapshots with their page metadata and defer redundant design checkpoints while uploads are busy.
  • Back off for HTTP 429 responses without a retry header and show pending uploads clearly in Test this visit.
  • Preserve existing recording payloads, privacy controls, settings and public design assets.

1.2.0

  • Preserve safe original styling, theme state, fonts and SVG geometry while retaining form-text and private-region masking.
  • Add reusable public asset snapshots for eligible images, backgrounds and fonts.
  • Load long replays in sections and remove the previous fixed per-recording storage cutoff.
  • Add owner-controlled storage budgets and manual retention; preserve existing settings on upgrade.

1.1.12

  • Fix large styled pages stopping before their first upload: compress recording batches and stored stylesheets without removing CSS rules.
  • Count new recordings as saved after receiving a page snapshot; distinguish monthly attempts and visits awaiting their first snapshot.
  • Keep privacy filtering, confirmed uploads, bounded retries and separate wire, expanded-data and hosting protections.

Earlier releases, including the 1.1.11 form-text privacy fix: changelog.txt.

upgrade_notice.1.2.6: Update Free first, then matched Pro without uninstalling. Clear page caches and reload open admin tabs. Existing recordings, settings and licence state remain. Test a new signed-out visit; earlier recordings cannot recover interactions that were never captured.
upgrade_notice.1.2.5: Update Free first, then matched Pro without uninstalling. Reload open admin tabs and clear page caches. Existing recordings, settings and licence state remain. Settings saves now require the revision supplied by GET /settings; reload old forms before saving.
upgrade_notice.1.2.4: Privacy and admission hardening. Update Free, then matched Pro without uninstalling. Cart and checkout now require an explicit masked-recording choice. Review visitor controls, clear caches and test a signed-out visit. Saved recordings remain; exports and backups need separate review.
upgrade_notice.1.2.3: Recording management improvements. Update Free first, then the matching Pro add-on without uninstalling. Cleanup is manual and requires a preview and confirmation.
upgrade_notice.1.2.2: The floating Replay privacy button is now off unless enabled in Settings. Use the switch or a #clickclue-privacy footer/menu link to offer the controls. Existing recording modes and saved visits remain. Clear page caches after updating.
upgrade_notice.1.2.1: Fix replay timing and reduce unnecessary recording requests. Clear page caches after replacing the plugin. A host rate limit can still block uploads; Test this visit now identifies HTTP 429. Saved recordings and settings remain in place.
upgrade_notice.1.2.0: Improved visual replay and long-visit playback. Existing settings remain. Enable public design asset capture if desired, clear caches and verify a signed-out replay. Keep Free 1.2.0 or newer for new replay assets and large recordings.
upgrade_notice.1.1.12: Fix large-page recording failures and clarify attempts versus saved replays. Update Free, clear page/CDN caches, then run a signed-out test. Earlier stored recordings remain available. Keep 1.1.12 or newer to replay newly compressed styles correctly.
upgrade_notice.1.1.11: Privacy fix for form text in capture, storage and replay. Older page text is masked; clicks, notes and bookmarks remain. Stored cleanup runs in batches. Backups/exports are not rewritten. Clear page/CDN caches.
